Report mandates (4 report mandates)

Statutory duties that require this agency to publish or file a report, with a City Record filing receipt when that report appears.

  • ◆Mandate · Issue a report on issues related to the Department of Correction’s grievance process; incorporate direct feedback from incarcerated individuals and proposed recommendations for relevant improvements; include recommendations on improving the grievance process for vulnerable populations; submit the report to the Council and post it on the Board’s website.
    report · deadline 2021-07-01 · every 3 years · Int. No. 1334-A, § 1, amending New York City Charter § 626(f) · Source law↗
  • ◆Mandate · Publish a preliminary report on its website for each death of an individual in custody, containing the statutorily specified information.
    report · deadline: No later than 10 days after such death, after allowing enough time for public notification · ongoing · NYC Charter § 626(i)(1) · Source law↗
  • ◆Mandate · Prepare a final report on each completed investigation, including recommendations and the names of involved Department and correctional-health employees.
    report · deadline: Upon conclusion of the investigation · ongoing · NYC Charter § 626(i)(2)(a) · Source law↗
  • ◆Mandate · Submit to the department and the council, and post on the board’s website, a report evaluating the department’s ability to provide persons in custody technology and support to securely receive and review evidence; incorporate direct feedback from people in custody and propose recommendations for improvements.
    report · deadline: By no later than one year after the effective date of this section · one-time · § 9-171(b) · Source law↗

Sources and measure definitions

  • PASSPort Public procurement records: registered contract values and counts are a point-in-time snapshot of current registered value, not actual spending.
  • Checkbook NYC, the Comptroller's spending ledger: actual payment amounts and transaction counts, not registered contract values.

These sources use different accounting scopes.
